title: Flatpak 1.18.6 fixes two vulnerabilities: setuid root files and a sandbox escape
summary: Flatpak maintainer Simon McVittie announced on oss-security that Flatpak 1.18.6 fixes two flaws. CVE-2026-133842 lets a compromised or malicious app, runtime or extension with extra-data create setuid root files on the host; CVE-2026-133845 lets a malicious app escape the sandbox through file descriptor passing in flatpak-portal. The advisory says all older releases should be assumed vulnerable. Neither page reports exploitation.
plain: Flatpak, the Linux app packaging system, has released 1.18.6 to fix two flaws that a malicious app could use to gain root-owned files or break out of its sandbox. Older releases are assumed to be affected.
exec: Two Flatpak flaws could let a malicious or compromised app gain setuid root files or escape its sandbox; the maintainers say all older releases should be assumed vulnerable.
action: The Flatpak advisory says to upgrade to Flatpak 1.18.6; older LTS distributions can backport the fixes, and Linuxiac says to update once your distribution ships patched packages.
date_note: The oss-security post and Linuxiac article are both dated 24 November; neither gives an earlier release day.

validation.note: The maintainer's own oss-security advisory and Linuxiac were read; both state the two flaws and the fixed release.

review.note: Compared CVEs, flaws, fixed version, advice, date and no-exploitation statement with the oss-security post and Linuxiac
